written.myAnswer: Elements with the same number of electrons in their outermost shell are placed in the same group.
No. Sodium is more reactive than calcium because sodium loses its single outermost electron more readily.
Group 16 and 17 elements have nearly complete outer shells and tend to accept electrons to complete their octets, so they have a strong attraction for electrons.
Oxygen has six outer-shell electrons and needs two to complete its octet. Accepting three would give it more than an octet, so it does not form O³⁻.
